The City of Tampa's North Franklin Street / Downtown designation lists buildings on this part of Franklin Street, including the Rialto Theatre (1924, 1617 N. Franklin St.), two Vintage Auto buildings (1920, 1609 and 1613 N. Franklin St.) and the Fariss Building (1920, 1701 N. Franklin St.).
heritage.visiting: Walk North Franklin Street north of Kay Street; the buildings are private businesses.

places.notes: Whether those City-designated buildings fall inside the NRHP boundary is not stated in the sources read.

places.name: Hampton Terrace Historic District
places.summary: A National Register residential district of Craftsman bungalows in Old Seminole Heights, roughly between Hanna Avenue, 15th Street, Hillsborough Avenue and Nebraska Avenue.

designations.name: National Register of Historic Places

heritage.story: The National Register lists the district for its community planning and architecture, with a period of significance from 1900 to 1949 and 1920 as a significant year. Wikipedia notes that it is one of two National Register districts in Old Seminole Heights, with the Seminole Heights Residential District.
heritage.visiting: A residential neighborhood; the houses are private.

places.notes: Thin record: only the NPGallery metadata was read (the nomination PDF was not). Area set to seminole-heights (Old Seminole Heights, per Wikipedia).

places.name: Home Association (Old People's Home)
places.summary: A 1924 Colonial Revival home for the elderly, built on land donated by Peter O. Knight for a charity founded in 1899 after two elderly women arrived at Tampa's train station with nowhere to stay.

designations.name: National Register of Historic Places
City of Tampa local historic landmark

heritage.story: In 1899 four women rented rooms at 405 Washington Street for two elderly women who had arrived at the station without lodging or family, and named the charity Kadesh Barnea, Hebrew for 'place of rest'. When it needed more room, Peter O. Knight donated the land for this building and a tree-filled park. The City of Tampa says it became the largest publicly supported home for the elderly in Tampa.
heritage.visiting: Exterior only.

places.notes: Current use not found. Woodlawn Cemetery has an Old People's Home memorial.

places.name: Dr. Jacob White, Sr. House
places.summary: A 1925 two-story brick Craftsman house built by Dr. Jacob White Sr., the first Black general practitioner in Tampa, and later home of his son, a tuberculosis physician.

designations.name: City of Tampa local historic landmark

heritage.story: Dr. Jacob White Sr. was the first Black general practitioner of medicine in Tampa. His son, Dr. Jacob White Jr., later lived here; the City of Tampa says he was the first and only Black doctor in Florida in the field of tuberculosis studies during his years of practice.
heritage.visiting: Exterior only.

places.name: Tierra del Lago Cigar Factory
places.summary: A 1908 blond brick cigar factory in Gary, east of Ybor City, designed by Fred J. James for W. H. Streeter's Tierra del Lago company, best known for its 'O U NO' clear Havana cigar.

heritage.style: Brick vernacular with Romanesque Revival brickwork

designations.name: City of Tampa local historic landmark

heritage.story: W. H. Streeter moved his cigar factory from Lakeland to Gary in 1908 and had Fred J. James, designer of several West Tampa factories, draw plans costing $3,000 for a three-and-a-half-story building. Gary Lodge No. 240, F&AM, moved in in 1921 and stayed until 1972.
heritage.visiting: Exterior only.

# history-tampa — historic sites and districts in Tampa (checked 2026-09-27)

## What this slice covers
71 places, each with a heritage block (built, architect, style, designations, era, story, visiting, sources), plus 72 rights-cleared Wikimedia Commons images (media) for 52 of them.

Counts by area: downtown-tampa 21, ybor-city 14, west-tampa 12, tampa-heights 8, north-tampa 3, davis-islands 3, east-tampa 3, seminole-heights 2, hyde-park 2, south-tampa 2, channel-district 1.
Counts by kind: historic-site 34, historic-district 8, landmark 7, park 6, house-of-worship 5, cemetery 4, sports 3, restaurant 2, performing-arts 1, attraction 1.

- **Ybor City**: the National Historic Landmark district; the Cuban Club, El Centro Español (NHL), Centro Asturiano, the Italian Club and La Unión Martí-Maceo; the V. M. Ybor factory (Ybor Square), El Pasaje (Cherokee Club), Parque Amigos de José Martí, Our Lady of Perpetual Help, Cuscaden Park and Pool, the Home Association, the 1937 Antifascist Women's March marker; heritage for the shared id columbia-restaurant-ybor-city.
- **Downtown / Channel District**: heritage for the shared id tampa-theatre; Old City Hall, the Kress building and the Woolworth sit-in site, Sacred Heart, St. Andrew's, the Henderson chapel (First Methodist), First Federal Savings (1963), Tampa Union Station, the Jackson Rooming House, North Franklin Street district, Masonic Temple No. 25, the Kennedy Boulevard (Lafayette Street) bridge, the Riverwalk Historical Monument Trail, Cotanchobee Fort Brooke Park, Plant Park and the Old School House at UT.
- **Central Avenue / The Scrub (Black history)**: Perry Harvey Sr. Park (Bro Bowl), Oaklawn Cemetery, St. Paul A.M.E., St. Peter Claver School, the Robert W. Saunders Sr. Library; plus Memorial Park Cemetery (East Tampa), the Buffalo Soldiers marker (Tampa Heights), Rogers Park Golf Course, the Fortune Taylor Bridge, Dr. Jacob White Sr. House, St. James House of Prayer.
- **Tampa Heights / Seminole Heights / North Tampa**: both historic districts plus Hampton Terrace and Upper North Franklin; the old Tampa Free Library, Woodlawn Cemetery, Old Hillsborough County High School, the Water Works building (heritage under the id ulele), the Sulphur Springs Water Tower, Babe Zaharias Golf Course.
- **West Tampa**: the district, El Centro Español de West Tampa, the Carnegie library, Fort Homer Hesterly Armory (now the Glazer JCC), the Sicilian Club, three cigar factories (Berriman-Morgan, Bustillo Brothers & Diaz, Balbin Brothers), MacFarlane Park, Martí-Colón Cemetery, the Céspedes Hall marker.
- **Hyde Park / South Tampa / Davis Islands**: Hyde Park district, Peter O. Knight Cottage, Stovall House, Palma Ceia Spring; Palace of Florence, Palmerin Hotel, Roy Jenkins Pool.

## How candidates were found
1. Wikipedia's NRHP lists for Tampa and Hillsborough County (wikitext parsed: every Tampa listing with its reference number, date and Commons image) — discovery only; every NRHP reference was then opened on NPGallery (npgallery.nps.gov/AssetDetail/NRIS/<ref>) for title and listing date.
2. The City of Tampa's 2024 book "Designated Local Historic Landmarks, Districts, Multiple Properties" (tampa.gov PDF, 118 pages, text-extracted): the four local districts, 61 landmarks and five multiple-property groupings, with construction year, style, architect, NRHP and local designation years for each. This is the main source for built/style/architect/designations.
3. The City's Soulwalk pages (historic markers, cemeteries) and Parks pages (Cotanchobee, Perry Harvey Sr., Oaklawn walking tour, four cemeteries, pools) — these publish hours and, for parks, GPS coordinates (geo_source "official").
4. Hillsborough County's "Historical Markers of Hillsborough" series (hcfl.gov): Cuban Club, Tampa Theatre, Woolworth sit-in, Babe Zaharias, Buffalo Soldiers, Céspedes Hall, Fortune Taylor Bridge, Palma Ceia Spring, 1937 march.
5. The NPS Ybor City NHL nomination text (74000641_text, 42 pages, text-extracted) and the NPS place page; fritzhand/history-of-tampa (js/data.js, js/ybor-data.js) as a map of sources (its mapEvents pointed to the NHL nomination, the Soulwalk markers and the City archive; I re-opened each cited page myself).
6. Visit Tampa Bay's "History Vault" blog and listings, the Ybor City Chamber's visitor pages (social clubs, museums), and each organization's own site (Cuban Club, Italian Club, Centro Asturiano, Centro Ybor, Centro Español de Tampa, Columbia, Sacred Heart parish, Friends of Tampa Union Station, Jackson House Foundation, Friends of the Riverwalk, HCPLC library pages, UT Plant Park, Glazer JCC, Tampa Sports Authority golf sites, Ulele).
WebSearch was exhausted for the session at the start (200-call budget used by other agents), so discovery relied on these lists and on direct fetches; curl (with the ft.py text extractor) was used for most pages, WebFetch where curl was blocked.

## Media
Commons files came from Wikipedia's NRHP list image fields, fritzhand/history-of-tampa's mediaAssets (Fort Brooke 1837 lithograph, Scrub aerial 1950, Centro Español 1914/1933/2015, Centro Asturiano 1947, Ybor streetcar c.1900, Martí 1893, Lafayette Street Bridge 1925, HABS Tampa Theatre 1978, Union Station, North Franklin, E. 7th Ave, J.C. Newman, Floridan, Tampa Bay Hotel) and Commons searches. Every file's license, creator, size and URL were read from the Commons API (extmetadata = what the File: page shows) on 2026-09-27; only public domain, CC0, CC BY and CC BY-SA were kept. Five media records illustrate ids owned by other slices: the places henry-b-plant-museum (Tampa Bay Hotel, 1902), j-c-newman-cigar-company (El Reloj) and american-victory-ship-mariners-museum, and the stays hotel-flor-tampa-downtown (Floridan) and le-meridien-tampa (1905 federal courthouse). The metadata for about 30 files was read through WebFetch of the same Commons API after the API rate-limited this machine; values were copied verbatim. Two photos of sculptures (the Martí statue, a Riverwalk bust) carry a note: the US has no freedom of panorama for sculpture. Places still without an image: st-paul-ame-church-tampa, st-peter-claver-catholic-school, woodlawn-cemetery-tampa, ulele, sicilian-club-west-tampa, berriman-morgan-cigar-factory, bustillo-brothers-diaz-cigar-factory, balbin-brothers-cigar-factory, cespedes-hall-marker, fortune-taylor-bridge, peter-o-knight-cottage, roy-jenkins-pool, cuscaden-park-pool, our-lady-of-perpetual-help-church-ybor, antifascist-womens-march-marker, memorial-park-cemetery-tampa, tom-henderson-memorial-chapel, dr-jacob-white-sr-house, tierra-del-lago-cigar-factory.

## Deliberately left out (and why)
- Owned by other slices, not duplicated: henry-b-plant-museum (Tampa Bay Hotel), ybor-city-museum-state-park (Ferlita Bakery and the casitas — the casita tour is covered there), j-c-newman-cigar-company (El Reloj, see-tampa already has a full heritage block), tampa-baseball-museum, tampa-firefighters-museum (Fire Station No. 1), sulphur-springs-museum, armature-works, american-victory ship, bayshore-boulevard, centennial-park-ybor, ritz-ybor, water-works-park; historic hotels are stays (Floridan = hotel-flor-tampa-downtown; the 1905 federal courthouse = le-meridien-tampa; Don Vicente Inn, Hotel Haya, Inn at El Reloj).
- Gone: the Old Union Depot Hotel (NRHP 2000) was demolished on May 23, 2010 (Wikipedia); Cespedes Hall survives only as a marker (included as the marker).
- Private houses and minor landmarks with nothing to see or no visitor angle: the ~20 NRHP-listed Davis Islands houses, Anderson-Frank, Hutchinson, Taliaferro, Leiman, Tampania, Guida, Robles, Captain W. P. Jackson and Costa houses, Biglow-Helms, Plant-Hatton, Souders, Seybold Bakery lofts, Metal Works-Dicus, Larmon warehouse, Strickland warehouse, Giunta farm, Tolle parsonage, Tippin water plant, Kid Mason Center, Roosevelt Elementary, Port Tampa's Commercial Bank and Old St. Mark, Zion Lutheran, Michigan Avenue (Columbus Drive) bridge, Spanish Apartments and Bay Isle building; Palmetto Beach district (NPGallery record garbled; not read).
- Not found on an official page: Zion Cemetery (rediscovered 2019; no visitor site found), the Dobyville and Jimi Hendrix Soulwalk markers (locations not published; Hendrix is at Curtis Hixon Park, a venues-bay record).
- Around the Bay (Plant City, Ruskin, Brandon, Temple Terrace, Fort Foster, Egmont Key, Cockroach Key) belongs to history-region.

## Open questions for the verifier
- Status semantics: exterior-only private buildings (El Pasaje, Kress, Stovall, Davis Islands buildings, cigar factories) and the Jackson House (not open; restoration stalled) are status "open" meaning the site can be seen; visiting says "exterior only". Tampa Union Station has a status_note about a renovation under way (train service continues). Cuscaden Pool is "seasonal" (closed for the season).
- Conflicts reported, not reconciled (see each record's notes): Cuban Club 1917 vs 1918; El Pasaje 1895 vs 1886; Martí-Maceo move 1960 vs 1966; Union Station NRHP date (Feb 2 vs Jun 5, 1974); Tampa Theatre constructed 1925 (City) vs opened 1926; Woolworth address 801 vs 901 N. Franklin; Fort Brooke arrival Jan 10 vs Jan 18, 1824; Old School House c. 1855 vs 1858; Old HCHS NRHP 2007 vs 2008; Hesterly 1941 vs 1938; Babe Zaharias developer Hamner vs Hammer.
- Sulphur Springs Water Tower: the City says NRHP 1989 but it is not in Wikipedia's NRHP list — find the reference or drop the designation. Cuscaden Park "NRHP 1990" likewise (probably the Ybor district boundary increase).
- Perry Harvey Sr. Park: the NRHP-listed 1979 bowl was demolished and replaced; check whether the listing still stands.
- Several facts rest on Wikipedia only (flagged in notes): Scientology ownership of the Ybor factory, El Pasaje's tenant, the Kress block's 2017 sale, Saunders Library's 2015 building and architect, Old Tampa Free Library's current tenant, Rogers Park history, Sacred Heart's architect.
- Shared ids: tampa-theatre (venues-bay), columbia-restaurant-ybor-city and ulele (eat-tampa) get heritage blocks here; addresses and coordinates match the other slices. The timeline slice also uses three of the same Commons files (Martí 1893, Ybor factory, HABS Tampa Theatre) as timeline media.
